title: Written formal Tagalog: letters and email
objectives: Open and close a formal letter or email with the correct conventional phrases
Use formal pronoun and address choices (kayo/ninyo/inyo, Ginoo/Ginang/Binibini, Kagalang-galang)
Write a formal complaint and a formal request with the standard move structure
Explain how written formal register differs from polite spoken Tagalog

grammar.title: The architecture of a formal letter
grammar.explanation:
Formal Tagalog correspondence follows a fixed skeleton. Heading: date (Ika-19 ng Agosto, 2026), then the addressee with title: G. RICARDO SANTOS (G. = Ginoo 'Mr.', Gng. = Ginang 'Mrs.', Bb. = Binibini 'Miss'). High officials get Kagalang-galang 'Honorable': Kagalang-galang na Alkalde ng Lungsod ng Maynila. The salutation is Mahal na Ginoo/Ginang or, addressing an office, Sa Kinauukulan 'To Whom It May Concern'.

The body opens by stating purpose at once: Ako po ay sumusulat upang... 'I am writing in order to...' or Ang liham pong ito ay may layuning... 'This letter has the purpose of...'. Notice the ay-inversion (Ako po ay sumusulat) — rare in speech, standard in formal writing.

Closings: Lubos na gumagalang, / Gumagalang, 'Respectfully yours', or Ang inyong lingkod 'Your servant'. Before it, a courtesy line: Maraming salamat po sa inyong pag-unawa at pagtugon 'Thank you for your understanding and response' or Umaasa po ako sa inyong agarang aksyon 'I hope for your prompt action.'

grammar.title: Formal pronouns and the ay-inversion on paper
grammar.explanation:
In formal writing you address the reader consistently as kayo/ninyo/inyo even when writing to one person — this is the written counterpart of the polite plural you learned for speech. Mixing ka and kayo in one letter is a register error; pick kayo and hold it. Refer to yourself with ako/ko plus po where the tone calls for it; official-to-official letters often drop po but keep kayo.

The ay-inversion (topic + ay + predicate) is the signature of written formal Tagalog: Ang inyong kahilingan ay naaprubahan — 'Your request has been approved.' In speech you'd say Naaprubahan na po ang kahilingan ninyo. Overusing ay in speech sounds stiff; underusing it in formal documents looks casual. Formal writing also prefers full words over contractions: hindi rather than 'di, at saka avoided in favor of at, ganoon over ganun.

Vocabulary shifts too: liham for sulat, tanggapan for opisina, paaralan for eskuwela, nais for gusto, ngunit/subalit for pero, sapagkat/dahil sa for kasi. You met most of these formal words in earlier units; a formal letter is where they all come out at once.

grammar.title: The complaint and the request: move by move
grammar.explanation:
A formal complaint (liham-reklamo) makes four moves. (1) Identify yourself and the transaction: Ako po si..., isang residente ng... / Bumili po ako ng... noong ika-5 ng Hulyo. (2) State the problem factually, using the causal language of Unit 5: Subalit, dalawang linggo na po ang nakalilipas, hindi pa rin dumarating ang produkto. (3) State what you want, with nais + object-focus verb: Nais ko pong hilingin ang agarang refund o kapalit na produkto. (4) Set a courteous expectation: Umaasa po akong matutugunan ito sa loob ng pitong araw.

A formal request (liham-kahilingan) is gentler: purpose first (Ako po ay sumusulat upang humiling ng...), then justification (sapagkat...), then the concrete ask with modest verbs: Malaki po ang maitutulong ninyo kung... 'It would help greatly if you...'; Kung maaari po sana ay... 'If it were possible...' — note sana softening the request, a use you can now connect to its irrealis meaning.

Keep both letter types free of idioms, exclamation points, and Taglish. Formal written Tagalog is conservative; the color you use in speech and social media stays at the door.

example.tl: Natanggap namin ang inyong liham noong ika-3 ng Agosto.
example.en: We received your letter on August 3.

vocab.note: standard salutation when the addressee is an office

example.tl: Sa Kinauukulan: Ako po ay sumusulat upang magreklamo.
example.en: To Whom It May Concern: I am writing to file a complaint.

vocab.note: abbreviated G.; Ginang (Gng.) = Mrs., Binibini (Bb.) = Miss

example.tl: Mahal na Ginoo: Isinusumite ko po ang aking aplikasyon.
example.en: Dear Sir: I am submitting my application.

vocab.note: used in addresses to officials: Kagalang-galang na Hukom

example.tl: Kagalang-galang na Alkalde, isang mapagpakumbabang kahilingan po ito.
example.en: Honorable Mayor, this is a humble request.

example.tl: Lubos na gumagalang, Maria Clara Reyes.
example.en: Respectfully yours, Maria Clara Reyes.

example.tl: Ang inyong lingkod, Jose P. Manalo.
example.en: Your servant, Jose P. Manalo.

vocab.note: nais ko pong... = I would like to...

example.tl: Nais ko pong humingi ng kopya ng aking rekord.
example.en: I would like to request a copy of my record.

example.tl: Hinihiling namin ang inyong agarang tugon.
example.en: We request your prompt response.

example.tl: Tinanggihan ng tanggapan ang kanyang kahilingan.
example.en: The office denied his request.

example.tl: Naghain siya ng pormal na reklamo laban sa tindahan.
example.en: He filed a formal complaint against the store.

example.tl: Maghahain kami ng reklamo sa munisipyo bukas.
example.en: We will file a complaint at the municipal hall tomorrow.

example.tl: Isumite ang lahat ng dokumento bago mag-alas-singko.
example.en: Submit all documents before five o'clock.

example.tl: Wala pa kaming natatanggap na tugon mula sa inyong tanggapan.
example.en: We have not yet received any response from your office.

example.tl: Tumugon ang kompanya makalipas ang tatlong linggo.
example.en: The company responded after three weeks.

example.tl: Kailangan po ng agarang aksyon sa problemang ito.
example.en: This problem needs prompt action.

example.tl: Umaasa akong matutugunan ang aming hinaing.
example.en: I hope our grievance will be addressed.

example.tl: Pinakinggan ng konseho ang mga hinaing ng mga magsasaka.
example.en: The council listened to the farmers' grievances.

vocab.note: salamat sa inyong pag-unawa = thank you for your understanding

example.tl: Salamat po sa inyong pag-unawa sa aming sitwasyon.
example.en: Thank you for your understanding of our situation.

example.tl: Humihingi po kami ng paumanhin sa naging abala.
example.en: We apologize for the inconvenience caused.

example.tl: Paumanhin po sa abalang idinulot ng aming pagkakamali.
example.en: Our apologies for the inconvenience our error caused.

example.tl: Kalakip po nito ang kopya ng resibo bilang patunay.
example.en: Attached herewith is a copy of the receipt as proof.

example.tl: Sumusulat po ako patungkol sa inyong anunsyo noong Lunes.
example.en: I am writing regarding your announcement last Monday.

example.tl: Wala silang naibigay na detalye hinggil sa iskedyul.
example.en: They gave no details concerning the schedule.

vocab.note: written register; spoken equivalents: dahil, kasi

example.tl: Hindi ako nakadalo sapagkat ako ay may sakit noon.
example.en: I was unable to attend because I was ill at the time.

example.tl: Isang mapagpakumbabang kahilingan po ito mula sa aming samahan.
example.en: This is a humble request from our association.

vocab.note: lumipas, lumilipas, lilipas; 'ang nakalipas' = the past

example.tl: Tatlong linggo na po ang lumipas mula nang magbayad ako.
example.en: Three weeks have passed since I paid.

example.tl: Inaprubahan ng punong-guro ang aming kahilingan.
example.en: The principal approved our request.

vocab.note: distinct from the verb samahan 'to accompany' — context decides

example.tl: Pinuno siya ng samahan ng mga magulang sa paaralan.
example.en: She heads the parents' association at the school.

dialogue.title: Tulong sa pagsulat ng liham-reklamo
dialogue.context: Nica asks her uncle Efren, a retired clerk, to help her draft a complaint letter about an undelivered appliance.

lines.speaker: Nica
lines.tl: Tito, tutulungan mo raw ako sa liham-reklamo? Isang buwan nang hindi dumarating ang binili kong ref.
lines.en: Tito, you said you'd help me with a complaint letter? The fridge I bought hasn't arrived in a month.

lines.speaker: Efren
lines.tl: Sige. Una: kanino mo ipapadala? Kung sa kompanya mismo, 'Sa Kinauukulan' ang bati mo.
lines.en: Sure. First: who are you sending it to? If to the company itself, your salutation is 'Sa Kinauukulan'.

lines.speaker: Nica
lines.tl: May pangalan ako ng manager — si Gng. Torres.
lines.en: I have the manager's name — Mrs. Torres.

lines.speaker: Efren
lines.tl: Mas mabuti. 'Mahal na Ginang Torres' ang gamitin mo. At tandaan: kayo at ninyo ang panghalip, hindi ikaw at mo.
lines.en: Even better. Use 'Mahal na Ginang Torres'. And remember: kayo and ninyo are your pronouns, not ikaw and mo.

lines.speaker: Nica
lines.tl: Ganito ba: 'Ako po ay sumusulat upang magreklamo hinggil sa refrigerator na binili ko noong ika-15 ng Hulyo'?
lines.en: Like this: 'I am writing to complain regarding the refrigerator I bought on July 15'?

lines.speaker: Efren
lines.tl: Tamang-tama. Pormal ang ay-inversion diyan. Tapos ilahad mo ang problema: petsa ng bayad, pangako nila, at kung ilang araw na ang lumipas.
lines.en: Exactly right. The ay-inversion is properly formal there. Then lay out the problem: date of payment, their promise, and how many days have passed.

lines.speaker: Nica
lines.tl: Isusulat ko rin bang galit na galit ako? Kasi totoo naman.
lines.en: Should I also write that I'm furious? Because it's true.

lines.speaker: Efren
lines.tl: Huwag. Sa liham-reklamo, ang datos ang dapat magalit para sa iyo. Sabihin mo na lang: 'Nais ko pong hilingin ang agarang paghahatid o buong refund.'
lines.en: Don't. In a complaint letter, the facts should do the getting-angry for you. Just say: 'I would like to request immediate delivery or a full refund.'

lines.speaker: Nica
lines.tl: May kalakip pala akong resibo. Paano ko babanggitin?
lines.en: Oh, and I'm attaching a receipt. How do I mention it?

lines.speaker: Efren
lines.tl: 'Kalakip po nito ang kopya ng opisyal na resibo bilang patunay ng aking pagbili.'
lines.en: 'Attached herewith is a copy of the official receipt as proof of my purchase.'

lines.speaker: Nica
lines.tl: At ang pagtatapos — 'Ingat lagi, Nica' ba?
lines.en: And the closing — 'Take care always, Nica'?

lines.speaker: Efren
lines.tl: Naku, hindi! Iyan ay para sa text sa kaibigan. 'Umaasa po ako sa inyong agarang tugon. Lubos na gumagalang, Nica Alvarez.'
lines.en: Goodness, no! That's for texting a friend. 'I look forward to your prompt response. Respectfully yours, Nica Alvarez.'

reading.title: Liham-reklamo sa pabrika ng tubig
reading.tl:
Ika-19 ng Agosto, 2026

G. ROBERTO DIMAGIBA
Tagapamahala, AquaPuro Water Station
Brgy. San Isidro, Lungsod ng Calamba

Mahal na Ginoong Dimagiba:

Ako po si Elena Marquez, residente ng Blk. 7, Lt. 12, Villa Esperanza Subdivision, at suki ng inyong istasyon ng tubig sa loob ng halos apat na taon.

Ako po ay sumusulat upang maghain ng pormal na reklamo hinggil sa kalidad ng tubig na inihatid sa aming tahanan noong ika-14 ng Agosto. Nang buksan po namin ang unang lalagyan, may kakaibang amoy at lasa ang tubig. Kinabukasan, nagkasakit ng tiyan ang dalawa kong anak. Bagaman hindi ko po masasabing tiyak na ang tubig ang sanhi, hindi rin po maikakailang ito lamang ang bago sa aming tahanan nang mga araw na iyon.

Dahil po dito, nais kong hilingin ang mga sumusunod: una, ang agarang pagpapalit ng tatlong lalagyang inihatid sa amin; ikalawa, ang kopya ng pinakahuling resulta ng pagsusuri ng inyong tubig; at ikatlo, ang paglilinis at pagsusuri ng inyong mga kagamitan, upang maiwasan ang katulad na pangyayari sa hinaharap.

Kalakip po nito ang kopya ng resibo ng aming huling pagbili. Umaasa po akong matutugunan ninyo ang liham na ito sa loob ng pitong araw. Maraming salamat po sa inyong pag-unawa.

Lubos na gumagalang,

ELENA MARQUEZ
reading.en:
August 19, 2026

MR. ROBERTO DIMAGIBA
Manager, AquaPuro Water Station
Brgy. San Isidro, Calamba City

Dear Mr. Dimagiba:

I am Elena Marquez, a resident of Blk. 7, Lt. 12, Villa Esperanza Subdivision, and a regular customer of your water station for almost four years.

I am writing to file a formal complaint regarding the quality of the water delivered to our home on August 14. When we opened the first container, the water had a strange smell and taste. The next day, two of my children suffered stomach aches. Although I cannot say with certainty that the water was the cause, it also cannot be denied that it was the only new thing in our home during those days.

Because of this, I would like to request the following: first, the immediate replacement of the three containers delivered to us; second, a copy of the most recent test results for your water; and third, the cleaning and inspection of your equipment, so that a similar incident can be avoided in the future.

Attached herewith is a copy of the receipt of our latest purchase. I hope you will act on this letter within seven days. Thank you very much for your understanding.

Respectfully yours,

ELENA MARQUEZ

exercises.prompt: You are writing to a company office without knowing anyone's name. The correct salutation is:
exercises.explain: Sa Kinauukulan ('To Whom It May Concern') is the standard salutation for an unnamed office. The others are conversational or worse.

exercises.prompt: Which pronoun set belongs in a formal letter to one person?
exercises.explain: Formal writing addresses even a single reader with the polite plural kayo/ninyo/inyo, held consistently through the letter.

exercises.prompt: Ako po ay sumusulat ___ maghain ng pormal na reklamo. (in order to — formal)
exercises.hint: the formal purpose conjunction from Unit 5
exercises.explain: The stock opening is Ako po ay sumusulat upang... — ay-inversion plus formal upang, the signature of the written register.

exercises.prompt: Which closing is appropriate for a formal request letter?
exercises.explain: Lubos na gumagalang ('Respectfully yours') is a standard complimentary close; the others belong to texts and casual notes.

exercises.prompt: ___ po nito ang kopya ng resibo bilang patunay. (Attached herewith)
exercises.hint: the formal word for an enclosure
exercises.explain: Kalakip nito = 'attached herewith'; it introduces enclosures in formal correspondence.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence shows correct formal ay-inversion?
exercises.explain: Ay-inversion places the topic first, then ay, then the predicate: Ang inyong kahilingan ay naaprubahan — 'Your request has been approved.'

exercises.tl: Umaasa po kami sa inyong agarang tugon hinggil sa aming kahilingan.
choices: They hope for a prompt response regarding their request.
They are angry that their request was denied.
They are withdrawing their request immediately.
They already received a response to their request.
exercises.explain: Umaasa sa agarang tugon = 'hoping for a prompt response'; hinggil sa aming kahilingan = 'regarding our request'. It's the standard courteous expectation line.

exercises.prompt: I would like to request a copy of my school record. (formal, with po)
exercises.answer: Nais ko pong hilingin ang kopya ng aking rekord sa paaralan.
accept: Nais ko pong hilingin ang kopya ng aking rekord sa paaralan
Nais ko pong humingi ng kopya ng aking rekord sa paaralan
Nais ko pong hilingin ang kopya ng rekord ko sa paaralan
exercises.explain: Nais replaces gusto in formal register; hilingin (object focus) targets the specific thing requested; paaralan is the formal word for school.

exercises.prompt: Humihingi po kami ng paumanhin sa abalang idinulot ng pagkaantala ng inyong padala.
exercises.answer: We apologize for the inconvenience caused by the delay of your shipment.
accept: We apologize for the inconvenience caused by the delay of your shipment
We ask your pardon for the inconvenience caused by the delay of your package
We apologize for the inconvenience that the delay of your delivery caused
exercises.explain: Humingi ng paumanhin = 'to apologize (formally)'; abalang idinulot ng... = 'inconvenience caused by...' — note idinulot, the i- verb of dulot from Unit 5.

exercises.prompt: Your complaint letter draft says: 'Sobrang galit na galit na ako kasi ang tagal-tagal n'yo!' What should you do?
choices: Keep it — honesty is best in complaints.
Rewrite it factually, e.g. 'Tatlong linggo na po ang lumipas mula nang magbayad ako.'
Translate it into English to sound more formal.
exercises.explain: Formal complaints let facts carry the force: state elapsed time and broken promises neutrally. Emotional outbursts, contractions (n'yo) and kasi are spoken-register items.

exercises.tl: Kinakailangan pong isumite ang lahat ng dokumento sa aming tanggapan bago matapos ang buwan.
choices: All documents must be submitted to their office before the end of the month.
The office will mail the documents at the end of the month.
Some documents may be submitted next month.
The office is closed until the end of the month.
exercises.explain: Kinakailangang isumite = 'must be submitted'; sa aming tanggapan = 'to our office'; bago matapos ang buwan = 'before the month ends'.

exercises.prompt: I am writing to file a formal complaint regarding the product I bought on August 5. (formal, with po)
exercises.answer: Ako po ay sumusulat upang maghain ng pormal na reklamo hinggil sa produktong binili ko noong ika-5 ng Agosto.
accept: Ako po ay sumusulat upang maghain ng pormal na reklamo hinggil sa produktong binili ko noong ika-5 ng Agosto
Sumusulat po ako upang maghain ng pormal na reklamo hinggil sa produktong binili ko noong ika-5 ng Agosto
Ako po ay sumusulat upang maghain ng pormal na reklamo patungkol sa produktong binili ko noong ika-5 ng Agosto
exercises.explain: The full formal opening: ay-inversion (optional but classic), upang for purpose, maghain ng reklamo 'to file a complaint', hinggil sa / patungkol sa 'regarding', and the formal date form ika-5 ng Agosto.
